Most people with Long COVID experience symptoms days after first learning they had COVID-19, but some people who later develop Long COVID do not know when they were infected.

related_questions.question: What are the health issues in Fiji?

text_blocks.snippet: Fiji faces several health challenges, including a high burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) like diabetes and heart disease, infectious diseases such as dengue fever, and issues related to access to healthcare, particularly in rural areas. Additionally, malnutrition, including both undernutrition and obesity, is a significant concern.
snippet_highlighted_words: a high burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) like diabetes and heart disease, infectious diseases such as dengue fever, and issues related to access to healthcare, particularly in rural areas

list.title: Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs):
list.snippet: NCDs like diabetes, cardiovascular diseases (including heart disease), and obesity are major causes of death and disability in Fiji. Many Fijians are not actively managing their health through lifestyle choices, leading to increased risk.
Dengue Fever: Fiji is prone to outbreaks of dengue fever, a mosquito-borne illness.
Other Mosquito-Borne Illnesses: Chikungunya and Zika virus are also concerns.
Typhoid and Leptospirosis: There are cases of typhoid and leptospirosis in Fiji, and travelers should be cautious of water and soil contamination.
HIV/AIDS: HIV/AIDS rates are rising, and the Fijian government has declared an outbreak.
Other Infections: Waterborne and foodborne illnesses are also prevalent.

list.title: Malnutrition:
list.snippet: Fiji experiences a double burden of malnutrition, with undernutrition (including micronutrient deficiencies) and overweight/obesity both affecting the population.

list.title: Healthcare Access:
list.snippet: While the constitution guarantees the right to health, access to quality healthcare, especially in rural and remote areas, can be limited due to under-resourcing and lack of infrastructure.

list.title: Lifestyle Choices:
list.snippet: Unhealthy diets, lack of physical activity, smoking, and excessive alcohol consumption contribute to the high rates of NCDs.

list.title: Environmental Factors:
list.snippet: Poor sanitation and access to clean water contribute to the spread of infectious diseases.

list.title: Socioeconomic Factors:
list.snippet: Poverty and lack of education can affect access to healthcare and healthy lifestyles.

list.title: Government Initiatives:
list.snippet: The Fijian Ministry of Health and Medical Services (MHMS) is working to address these health challenges through various initiatives, including promoting healthy lifestyles, improving healthcare access, and controlling infectious diseases.

list.title: WHO Collaboration:
list.snippet: The World Health Organization (WHO) is also involved in supporting Fiji's efforts to improve health outcomes.

list.title: Vaccinations:
list.snippet: Ensure vaccinations are up-to-date, including those for Hepatitis A and B, Typhoid, and MMR.

list.title: Mosquito Protection:
list.snippet: Use insect repellent, cover up with clothing, and avoid mosquito-prone areas, particularly during outbreaks of dengue fever and Zika virus.

list.title: Food and Water Safety:
list.snippet: Avoid drinking tap water and be cautious about food hygiene.

list.title: Kava Consumption:
list.snippet: Be aware of the potential risks associated with kava, especially if mixed with other substances or if you have underlying health conditions.
